item.title: CHCC receives notice rescinding prior termination communication from SAMHSA - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: (CHCC) — On Jan. 14, 2026, the Commonwealth Healthcare Corporation received a termination notice under 2 CFR §200.340(a)(4) from the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration related to specific grant funding.

item.title: NMC Spring 2026 classes to stay on the As Terlaje campus; add/drop period extended through Jan. 30 - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: (NMC) — Northern Marianas College is reminding all students that classes will remain on the As Terlaje campus when the Spring 2026 term starts on Tuesday, Jan. 20. The college is also extending the add/drop period until Jan. 30, which will give returning/admitted students more time to register for classes.

item.title: CNMI expands Operation Governor’s Digital Connect to support manamko’ - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: (Office of the Governor) — Under the leadership of Gov. David M. Apatang and Lt. Gov. Dennis C. Mendiola, the Office of the Governor — in partnership with the Department of Community and Cultural Affairs’ Office of Aging and the CNMI Broadband Policy and Development Office — is proud to announce the expansion of Operation Governor’s Digital Connect to include the manamko’ across all three islands of the Commonwealth.

item.title: King-Hinds: CNMI employers can seek H-1B visa fee exemptions - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: THE U.S. Department of Homeland Security has informed U.S. Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds that CNMI employers can request an exemption from the $100,000 H-1B visa application fee that President Donald Trump imposed via executive order last year.

item.title: NMI honors Sugar King’s legacy - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: THE NMI Museum of History and Culture opened a special commemorative exhibit on Thursday, Jan. 15 to mark the 150th birthday of Haruji Matsue, the “Sugar King” whose early 20th-century sugar industry transformed Saipan’s economy and landscape.

item.title: Orsini wants Hopwood construction to move forward - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: BOARD of Education member Andrew Orsini wants the construction of Admiral Herbert G. Hopwood Middle School to move forward without further delay.

item.title: Governor to form revenue council - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: GOVERNOR David M. Apatang on Thursday invited other CNMI officials and business community leaders to participate in a Governor’s Revenue Council he is establishing in response to fiscal reform policies submitted by a committee he created last year to develop plans for a balanced budget.

item.title: Sirok: CUC has not submitted petition to lift FAC stabilization order - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: COMMONWEALTH Public Utilities Commission Chairman James Sirok said the Commonwealth Utilities Corporation has not yet submitted a petition to lift the current Fuel Adjustment Charge stabilization order, which the CPUC would need before issuing a decision.

item.title: Lijie Cui asks for temporary release amid removal proceedings - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: LIJIE Cui, the former majority shareholder of Imperial Pacific International, asked the Saipan Immigration Court to set a monetary bond for her temporary release while removal proceedings continue.

item.title: ‘Contracting population equals contracting economy,’ says Labor chief - Marianas Variety News & Views
item.description: A CONTRACTING population will continue to shrink the local economy, CNMI Labor Secretary Leila Staffler said, underscoring the need for both returning residents and a stable foreign-worker pipeline as federal officials weigh the future of the CW program.
